before:
In a Cursor chat, run:

```text
/add-plugin pstack
```

Cursor confirms the plugin is installed.

In Claude Code, run `/plugin marketplace add cursor/plugins`, then `/plugin install pstack@cursor-plugins`. Claude Code prefixes plugin commands, so each command in this guide takes a `pstack:` prefix there, such as `/pstack:setup-pstack`, which writes its model rule to `~/.claude/rules/pstack-models.md`. The [Claude Code adapter](../harness/claude-code.md) covers the other differences.
after:
From this repository, install and validate the separate OpenCode profile:

```sh
./scripts/install/pstack.sh
./scripts/doctor/pstack.sh
```

Then run `oc-pstack` in the project you want to work on. It uses this profile's native plugin, skills and isolated session database. The [profile README](../../README.md) states the current installation and verification status; do not treat an unfinished checkout as a released installation.
reason: 설치 과정을 저장소의 별도 OpenCode 실행기로 교체한다.

before: [`/setup-pstack`](../../skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md) detects the models you have access to, asks for a reasoning budget, shows you each role (code delegates, judgment, the review panels), and asks what you want. Answer the questions. It writes `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc`, a small rule every pstack skill reads.
after: [`/setup-pstack`](../../skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md) detects available native models, asks for a reasoning budget, shows every role and panel, and asks what you want. Answer the questions. It writes `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/pstack-models.json`; each native subagent invocation resolves its required role from that file.
reason: 설정 위치와 실제 호출 시 적용되는 저장 방식을 명시한다.

before: You only override what you care about. A role with no line in the rule keeps the skill's default. To restore a default, delete that role's line. A rerun of `/setup-pstack` keeps any role whose model differs from the default. When a default changes, a rule written before the change still pins the old default, so delete those role lines, or delete the file, then run `/setup-pstack` again.
after: You only override what you care about. A missing role key keeps the skill default. To restore a default, delete that role key. Rerunning `/setup-pstack` keeps deliberate changes to model families, lists and aliases. An explicitly saved old default stays pinned; delete its key, or the file, then run setup again to adopt defaults.
reason: 부분 역할 설정과 삭제를 통한 기본값 복구를 JSON 형식으로 보존한다.

before: You might be wondering what happens if you use Auto. Set a role to `inherit-parent` or `auto` and pstack omits the subagent `model` field, so the subagent inherits your parent chat model. Both values mean the same thing, and neither is a model slug. For a panel role the value is a list, and one subagent runs per entry, so the list length sets the panel size. Setup also configures `swarm workers`, the default model for every `/swarm` worker unless a race names a model for each arm.
after: Set a role to `inherit-parent` or `auto` to run on the parent chat model. Both aliases mean the same thing and are not provider model IDs. The native role executor resolves the parent model explicitly so a subagent's own agent default cannot override that choice. Panel lists preserve order and duplicates and create one seat per entry. Setup also configures `swarm workers`, the default unless a comparison assigns a model to an arm.
reason: 부모 모델 상속과 패널 좌석 의미를 실제 native 동작에 맞게 설명한다.

before: From here you can type normal follow-ups. To keep `/poteto-mode` on for the whole chat, pick it from the `/` menu with Option+Enter (Mac) or Alt+Enter (Windows) instead of Enter. That makes it a [Custom Mode](https://cursor.com/docs/skills#using-a-skill-as-a-custom-mode), which stays in context on every turn until you exit it. Custom Modes are available in the Agents Window and the CLI. Plain Enter attaches the skill to one message, and it fades as the chat moves on.
after: From here you can type normal follow-ups. For a persistent mode, run `/pstack-mode on poteto-mode`, then send the task. Native session instructions keep the full skill active on every turn, through compaction and service restarts. `/pstack-mode off` removes it and `/pstack-mode status` reports the selection. Plain `/poteto-mode` loads the skill for that request rather than enabling a persistent mode.

before: If you run several agents against one repository on one computer, they will fight over the working tree, the ports, and the build output. The cleanest isolation is a [cloud subagent](https://cursor.com/docs/subagents#cloud-subagents). Each one gets its own VM and branch, so it can install dependencies, run your app, and record video of the result without touching your machine. Type `/in-cloud` before the task, or ask the parent chat to hand work to cloud subagents.
after: If several agents share one computer, they can collide on the working tree, ports and build output. A separate VM and branch for each worker isolates dependencies, application processes and recordings too. Native OpenCode subagents run on their host; this profile does not provision hosted VMs. When a workflow requires a separate machine, keep that requirement and mark it blocked until an actual remote execution environment is configured. A local worktree is not a VM.
reason: 별도 VM의 요구를 유지하고 미제공 실행 기반을 명시한다. 로컬 worktree와 동등하다고 주장하지 않는다.

before: [`/no-comments`](../../skills/no-comments/SKILL.md) spawns [Comment Sicko](../../agents/comment-sicko.md), a read-only reviewer with a short keep list: license headers, doc comments on a public API, links that explain what code can't, behavior forced by an external dependency you can't reshape. Everything else goes. A surprise in your own code gets no such pass. The comment comes back as a refactor flag, and `/no-comments` fixes the flags it accepts at the root cause. When a comment claims a constraint, "do not remove", the skill offers to encode the claim as a type, test, or lint. Either way, the comment comes out.

before: - `/loop` is Cursor's built-in wake mechanism, not a pstack skill. The [Autonomous run playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/autonomous-run.md) uses it to re-check the finish condition on events or a heartbeat.
after: - `/loop` uses native `pstack_schedule` wakes. A fixed interval repeats on that cadence; without one the agent chooses a useful delay or event. The [Autonomous run playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/autonomous-run.md) rechecks the finish condition on events or a heartbeat. Wakes persist across service restarts, but the host and OpenCode background service must be running. `/loop stop` cancels the session's schedules.

before: To stop a run on purpose, tell the agent to pause, or that you're about to go offline or restart Cursor. The [Pause safely playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/pause-safely.md) finishes or backs out of the current step, commits a work-in-progress checkpoint, and writes a resume note. A fresh chat picks the work up from that note through the Session pickup playbook. Saying "keep going" never triggers a pause.
after: To stop a run on purpose, tell the agent to pause, or that you're about to go offline or restart OpenCode. The [Pause safely playbook](../../skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/pause-safely.md) finishes or backs out of the current step, commits a work-in-progress checkpoint, and writes a resume note. A fresh chat picks the work up from that note through the Session pickup playbook. Saying "keep going" never triggers a pause.

before: A [Cursor Project](https://cursor.com/blog/projects) gives one coordinator agent a persistent thread. The coordinator doesn't write code. It directs subagents, which run in the cloud by default, so the work continues when your laptop is closed. That's the shape the Orchestrate playbook expects. Start your prompts to the coordinator with `/poteto-mode`, and the subagents it spawns follow the playbooks.
after: Use a persistent OpenCode coordinator session for each program. The coordinator directs workers and does not write code. Run the OpenCode service on a host that remains online if work must continue while your laptop is closed. Hosted project dashboards and automatic cloud VM workers are not supplied by this profile; a workflow that requires them must remain blocked until an equivalent environment is available. Start coordinator tasks with `/poteto-mode` and enable a persistent mode with `/pstack-mode on poteto-mode`.
reason: 상주 조정자와 오프라인 운영 조건을 보존하고 호스팅된 Project/VM의 부재를 명시한다.

before: - Give each body of work its own Project, such as a feature, a migration, a perf push, or a tech-debt cleanup. Several can run side by side.
after: - Give each body of work its own persistent coordinator session, such as a feature, migration, perf push or tech-debt cleanup. Keep each program's ownership and state separate.

before: - Drag related chats into the Project, finished ones included. They become context for every agent in it.
after: - Preserve related session IDs and finished work as program evidence. Give workers explicit evidence pointers; do not claim that a hosted project dashboard has automatically shared context. Full workspace history is available through `pstack_history`.
